decomposition.meaning: Exact path: lower e with CD0 held, then refit CD0 once to preserve the 325-mph historical speed. Not a derivative or causal measurement.

turnSensitivity.perturbationDisclaimer: These +/-5% or +/-10% perturbations diagnose sensitivity; they are not historical error bars or permissible aircraft-to-aircraft adjustments.

decision.propulsion: Profile C yields the lowest held-out speed error on both Allied planes under equal single-anchor refits. This is cross-aircraft model discrimination, not a measured propeller map.
decision.inducedDrag: No F4-specific calibrated low-speed polar is validated. The 4-minute Rechlin clue and Greg worksheet cannot independently establish an Oswald factor; wrong gear ratio previously created a misleading 3:59 coincidence.
decision.currentBaseline: Keep F4 generic e=.78 provisional in interactive UI and preserve Greg-derived e=.558 as explicit sensitivity case, rather than artificially narrowing a band.
decision.limit: F4 emergency power documented to 15748ft, combat to 16076ft; 27000ft F4 comparisons remain unavailable.

historicalP47BCheck.caveat: Both candidates share the same P47B engine/prop assumptions. CD0 B-anchor was fitted at 5000 ft; other altitudes are withheld from that one-point fit. Source engine curves may nevertheless use the same test series.

p47Controlled.note: This is a controlled power/drag experiment, not a claim that P-47B and D-28 installations are historically drag-identical. Canopy, propeller, cooling and test configuration can alter aircraft-level CD0 despite common wing geometry.

ramPredictive.method: No climb MAP inputs: ideal, isentropic inlet-total-pressure ratio p0=p(1+0.2M^2)^3.5 at sourced full-throttle critical point; regulator caps rated MAP; speed-dependent BHP proportional to predicted manifold pressure relative to measured maximum-speed TAS, or explicit engine-chart rated MAP when no exact-altitude speed anchor exists.

mustang2200Ft.interpretation: 75-inHg low-gear CLIMB critical altitude is 2,200ft in the original report; the LEVEL-FLIGHT 75-inHg low-gear critical altitude is 7,400ft. At representative climb TAS 195mph the modeled regulator holds full MAP. The climb residual remains in prop/drag/weight/engine chart, not a demonstrated ram-pressure shortfall. Source climb TAS unreported; modeled optimum and takeoff mass are assumptions.

criticalFindings: C power/advance curve reproduces some OCR run η better than others; generic Cp mapping is not validated for 714 blade.
The measured climb efficiency loss with increased power is much larger than the difference currently produced by C in these representative power/RPM scenarios.
The provisional OCR point coefficients meet eta=J*Ct/Cp to rounding, but no original graphic/PDF scan was available to validate reading.
1946 E6K26 6507A-2 is a different propeller blade family and should NOT be pooled with Curtiss 714 as a single empirical propeller map.
NACA 1943 F2A turning report is only a method/metadata fixture until measured curves are read from the actual report images.
